sections.overview: The Egyptian Vulture is a member of the vulture family Accipitridae; its French name is Vautour percnoptère.
sections.identification: Adults have a bare yellow head and throat, pale body plumage and contrasting dark flight feathers.
sections.habitat: It uses open country, rocky slopes and escarpments across a range extending from southwestern Europe and Africa into Asia.
sections.diet: Carrion is central to its diet, but it also takes small prey, eggs, insects and other food.
sections.behavior: It is known to use stones to crack large eggs, a rare example of tool use in birds.
sections.reproduction: The regional and conservation summaries consulted here do not provide enough detail for a reliable account of its breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: As a relatively small vulture, it can feed on small remains and varied resources that larger carcass-feeders may leave behind.
sections.conservation: The IUCN Red List lists it as Endangered, with declines linked to poisoning, persecution and other pressures across parts of its range.
